The expected values come from the plan's decisions (30-day grace period, merge keeps both, account delete handled like its transactions' delete) and from the handler contracts, not from running the code.\n\n## Design decisions\n\n### Undo for removing an attachment\n\n- **Chosen: an \"Undo\" button in the notification after a removal, backed by a soft remove and `attachment-restore`.** Attachment rows are written without sync messages (#154), and the app's undo stack only records sync messages, so Ctrl/Cmd+Z can't see them.\n- **Alternative: put attachment changes on the app's undo stack.** That means writing the rows through sync messages, which the server-storage issue will rework anyway.\n- **Consequences:** Ctrl/Cmd+Z doesn't undo a removal; the notification's Undo does, for 10 seconds. The issue text still says \"the app's normal undo\" and should be updated.\n\n### When files are removed\n\n- **Chosen: 30 days after the delete or removal, tracked with a `deleted_at` stamp on the row.** The app's own undo history is cleared every time a budget opens, so the grace period isn't for that. It covers deletes that arrive by sync from another device, and re-downloading a budget, which replaces the rows but leaves the files.\n- **Alternative: work out delete times from `messages_crdt`.** More complicated, and it doesn't cover attachment rows, which don't sync.\n- **Consequences:** a deleted transaction's files take up space for 30 days. Files with no row wait 30 days too, which keeps a re-download from losing them the same day.\n\n### When cleanup runs\n\n- **Chosen: after the budget opens, without blocking it.** Next to the backup service would have been the obvious place, but that only runs outside the browser, and mobile runs in the browser.\n- **Alternative: a timer.** It adds a moving part for little gain, since budgets are opened often.\n- **Consequences:** a budget that is never reopened is never cleaned up.\n\n### Merging\n\n- **Chosen: move the dropped transaction's attachments to the kept one.**\n- **Alternative: leave them on the dropped transaction.** They would be hidden, then removed after the grace period, so the user would lose them.\n- **Consequences:** undoing a merge brings the dropped transaction back, but its attachments stay on the kept one, because the undo stack can't see attachment rows. Nothing is lost by the undo itself. Sync attachments across devices, add mobile support, and handle deletes and cleanup
## Summary

#154 lets a user attach and view files on desktop, stored on this device only. This sub-issue of #150 adds attachments to the mobile layout, and defines what happens to attachments when a transaction, account or budget is deleted or the delete is undone. It also removes attachment files on the device that nothing points to anymore.

**Rescoped:** attachments are still stored on the device only. Syncing attachments between devices, offline behavior, sync conflicts, and cleanup on the server moved to #NEW, which comes after this issue and #156.

## User Story

As a user who records expenses on my phone, I want to attach and view receipts there too, and I want my receipts to stay with a transaction if I delete it by mistake and undo, so that I don't lose proof of an expense.

## User Scenario

Ana pays for lunch with a client and opens Actual on her phone. She opens the transaction, taps "Attach," takes a photo of the receipt, and a paperclip appears on the transaction. Later she deletes a duplicate transaction by mistake, undoes the delete, and the receipt is still attached. Weeks after she deletes an old transaction on purpose, its receipt file is removed from her phone so it doesn't take up space.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Mobile**
- On mobile, transactions with attachments show an indicator in the transaction list.
- On mobile, a user can view a transaction's attachments, with file name and size, and open one. Images are shown in a preview; PDFs open in a new tab or the device's viewer.
- On mobile, a user can add an attachment from the camera or from files.
- Mobile has the same type and size checks as desktop (JPEG, PNG, WebP, PDF; 10 MB; no empty files), and shows the same error messages.
- On mobile, a user can remove an attachment, after confirming.
- The warning that files are kept in this browser only is shown on mobile too. **(proposed: also mention that some phones clear site data for apps that aren't used for a while)**
- Attaching from a split child attaches to its parent, as on desktop.

**Delete and undo**
- Deleting a transaction hides its attachments: they no longer appear in counts, indicators or lists. The files stay on the device.
- Undoing the delete restores the attachments, and they still open.
- Removing a single attachment can be undone with the app's normal undo. **(proposed; today it is confirmed but can't be undone)**
- When two transactions are merged, the kept transaction keeps the attachments of both. **(proposed)**

**Deleting accounts and budgets**
- Deleting an account handles the attachments of its transactions the same way as deleting those transactions. **(behavior pending customer decision)**
- Deleting a budget from this device removes its attachment files.

**Cleanup on this device**
- Attachment files and rows for transactions that were deleted more than a grace period ago are removed. **(proposed: 30 days, so undo is safe)**
- Files in the budget's `attachments/` folder that no attachment row points to are removed. This includes files restored from an import that no row uses.
- Cleanup never removes a file that a live attachment row points to.
- Cleanup can run again safely, and a failed or interrupted run leaves no data in a broken state.

## Out of Scope

- Uploading files to the sync server, syncing attachments between devices, offline behavior, sync conflicts, and cleanup on the server (#NEW)
- Search, filters, and bulk export (#156)
- OCR, cloud storage services, and importing attachments from other apps (out of scope for #150)

## Open Questions

- How long after a transaction is deleted can its attachment files be removed?
- What happens to attachments when an account is deleted or closed?
- When transactions are merged, should attachments from both be kept?
- Should removing a single attachment be undoable?
- When should cleanup run: when the budget opens, on a timer, or both?

## Rough Scope

**Medium.** Areas this touches: the mobile transaction UI (indicator, attachments screen, camera and file picker, viewer), transaction delete/undo and merge in loot-core, and a cleanup step for the budget's `attachments/` folder. Note that #154 writes attachment rows without sync messages, so undo for removing an attachment needs its own handling. #NEW will rework these rows to sync, so keep that path simple.

import * as fs from '#platform/server/fs';
import { logger } from '#platform/server/log';
import * as db from '#server/db';
import * as prefs from '#server/prefs';

import {
  getAttachmentsDir,
  isSafeAttachmentId,
  removeAttachmentFile,
  TEMP_SUFFIX,
} from './storage';

// Removes attachment rows and files that nothing uses anymore (#155):
// removed attachments, the attachments of deleted transactions, files that
// no row points to, and leftover temporary files. Everything is kept for a
// grace period first. That isn't for the app's undo, which is cleared each
// time a budget opens: it covers deletes that arrive by sync from another
// device, and a re-download, which replaces db.sqlite (and so the rows) but
// leaves the files.
//
// Each step can be interrupted at any point and leaves things consistent:
// rows are always removed before their files, so no row ever points at a
// file that cleanup removed.

export const ATTACHMENT_GRACE_MS = 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

// Files in attachments/ that have no row, and when cleanup first saw each
// one: { [id]: firstSeenMs }. The browser fs can't tell when a file was
// last modified, so cleanup keeps track itself.
const UNUSED_FILES_NAME = '.cleanup.json';

// Whether the attachment's transaction is live. Attachments belong to
// non-child transactions; the child case matches `resolveOwnerTransactionId`
// in case a row from an imported budget points at one.
const TRANSACTION_IS_LIVE = `EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM transactions t
    LEFT JOIN transactions p ON p.id = t.parent_id
    WHERE t.id = transaction_attachments.transaction_id
      AND t.tombstone = 0
      AND (COALESCE(t.isChild, 0) = 0 OR (p.id IS NOT NULL AND p.tombstone = 0))
)`;

export type AttachmentCleanupResult = {
  // Rows first seen as unused (removed, or their transaction deleted)
  stamped: number;
  // Rows whose transaction is live again
  unstamped: number;
  // Rows removed, with their files
  purged: number;
  // Files with no row, or leftover temporary files, removed
  removedFiles: number;
};

export async function cleanUpAttachments(
  budgetId: string,
  {
    now = Date.now(),
    graceMs = ATTACHMENT_GRACE_MS,
  }: { now?: number; graceMs?: number } = {},
): Promise<AttachmentCleanupResult> {
  const result: AttachmentCleanupResult = {
    stamped: 0,
    unstamped: 0,
    purged: 0,
    removedFiles: 0,
  };
  const cutoff = now - graceMs;

  // The database is whichever budget is open, so stop if that changes
  const isOpen = () => prefs.getPrefs()?.id === budgetId;

  if (!isOpen()) {
    return result;
  }
  try {
    Object.assign(result, stampRows(now));
  } catch (error) {
    logger.warn('Attachment cleanup: failed to stamp rows', error);
  }

  if (!isOpen()) {
    return result;
  }
  try {
    result.purged = await purgeRows(budgetId, cutoff);
  } catch (error) {
    logger.warn('Attachment cleanup: failed to remove rows', error);
  }

  if (!isOpen()) {
    return result;
  }
  try {
    result.removedFiles = await removeUnusedFiles(budgetId, {
      now,
      cutoff,
      isOpen,
    });
  } catch (error) {
    logger.warn('Attachment cleanup: failed to remove unused files', error);
  }

  return result;
}

// Step 1. `deleted_at` on a live row (`tombstone = 0`) means its transaction
// was deleted; on a removed row it is when it was removed. Recording when a
// delete was first noticed avoids reading `messages_crdt`.
function stampRows(now: number) {
  const stamped = db.runQuery(
    `UPDATE transaction_attachments SET deleted_at = ?
       WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
         AND (tombstone = 1 OR NOT ${TRANSACTION_IS_LIVE})`,
    [now],
  );
  // The delete was undone. Only live rows: a removed attachment keeps its
  // removal time even though its transaction is live, or it would never be
  // purged.
  const unstamped = db.runQuery(
    `UPDATE transaction_attachments SET deleted_at = NULL
       WHERE tombstone = 0 AND deleted_at IS NOT NULL
         AND ${TRANSACTION_IS_LIVE}`,
  );
  return {
    stamped: Number(stamped.changes),
    unstamped: Number(unstamped.changes),
  };
}

// Step 2. Rows first, then files. A file left behind if removing it fails is
// picked up by step 3 later.
async function purgeRows(budgetId: string, cutoff: number): Promise<number> {
  // The select and the delete run with nothing awaited in between, so both
  // see the same database
  const condition = `deleted_at IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at <= ?
    AND (tombstone = 1 OR NOT ${TRANSACTION_IS_LIVE})`;
  const rows = db.runQuery<{ id: string }>(
    `SELECT id FROM transaction_attachments WHERE ${condition}`,
    [cutoff],
    true,
  );
  if (rows.length === 0) {
    return 0;
  }
  db.runQuery(`DELETE FROM transaction_attachments WHERE ${condition}`, [
    cutoff,
  ]);

  for (const { id } of rows) {
    if (!isSafeAttachmentId(id)) {
      continue;
    }
    try {
      await removeAttachmentFile(budgetId, id);
    } catch (error) {
      logger.warn(`Attachment cleanup: failed to remove file ${id}`, error);
    }
  }
  return rows.length;
}

// Steps 3 and 4. A file with no row is removed once it has had no row for
// the whole grace period. A temporary file is removed the next time cleanup
// finds it, rather than straight away, so a save in progress isn't disturbed.
async function removeUnusedFiles(
  budgetId: string,
  {
    now,
    cutoff,
    isOpen,
  }: { now: number; cutoff: number; isOpen: () => boolean },
): Promise<number> {
  const dir = getAttachmentsDir(budgetId);
  if (!(await fs.exists(dir))) {
    return 0;
  }

  const names = await fs.listDir(dir);
  const firstSeen = await readUnusedFiles(dir);
  if (!isOpen()) {
    return 0;
  }
  // All rows, removed ones included: their files are step 2's to remove
  const rowIds = new Set(
    db
      .runQuery<{
        id: string;
      }>('SELECT id FROM transaction_attachments', [], true)
      .map(row => row.id),
  );

  const nextFirstSeen: Record<string, number> = {};
  let removed = 0;
  for (const name of names) {
    const isTemp = name.endsWith(TEMP_SUFFIX);
    const id = isTemp ? name.slice(0, -TEMP_SUFFIX.length) : name;
    // Also skips the list of unused files itself
    if (!isSafeAttachmentId(id) || (!isTemp && rowIds.has(id))) {
      continue;
    }

    const seen = firstSeen[name];
    const isDue = isTemp ? seen != null : seen != null && seen <= cutoff;
    if (!isDue) {
      nextFirstSeen[name] = seen ?? now;
      continue;
    }
    try {
      await fs.removeFile(fs.join(dir, name));
      removed++;
    } catch (error) {
      logger.warn(`Attachment cleanup: failed to remove file ${name}`, error);
      nextFirstSeen[name] = seen;
    }
  }

  await writeUnusedFiles(dir, firstSeen, nextFirstSeen);
  return removed;
}

async function readUnusedFiles(dir: string): Promise<Record<string, number>> {
  const path = fs.join(dir, UNUSED_FILES_NAME);
  try {
    if (!(await fs.exists(path))) {
      return {};
    }
    const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(path));
    const result: Record<string, number> = {};
    if (parsed != null && typeof parsed === 'object') {
      for (const [name, seen] of Object.entries(parsed)) {
        if (typeof seen === 'number') {
          result[name] = seen;
        }
      }
    }
    return result;
  } catch (error) {
    // Starting over only delays removing files, so that's safe
    logger.warn('Attachment cleanup: ignoring an unreadable list', error);
    return {};
  }
}

async function writeUnusedFiles(
  dir: string,
  previous: Record<string, number>,
  next: Record<string, number>,
) {
  const path = fs.join(dir, UNUSED_FILES_NAME);
  const isEmpty = Object.keys(next).length === 0;
  if (JSON.stringify(previous) === JSON.stringify(next)) {
    return;
  }
  if (isEmpty) {
    if (await fs.exists(path)) {
      await fs.removeFile(path);
    }
    return;
  }
  await fs.writeFile(path, JSON.stringify(next));
}

import { transactionAttachmentCountsQuery } from '@actual-app/core/shared/attachments';
import type { TransactionAttachmentCount } from '@actual-app/core/shared/attachments';
import type { TransactionEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';

import { useQuery } from './useQuery';

const EMPTY_COUNTS: ReadonlyMap<TransactionEntity['id'], number> = new Map();

// The number of attachments on each transaction, keyed by transaction id.
// Attachments on a split belong to the parent, so only parents and plain
// transactions appear. Updates live when attachments are added or removed.
export function useTransactionAttachmentCounts(): ReadonlyMap<
  TransactionEntity['id'],
  number
> {
  const { data } = useQuery<TransactionAttachmentCount>(
    () => transactionAttachmentCountsQuery(),
    [],
  );

  if (data == null || data.length === 0) {
    return EMPTY_COUNTS;
  }

  const counts = new Map<TransactionEntity['id'], number>();
  for (const row of data) {
    if (row.transaction_id != null && row.count > 0) {
      counts.set(row.transaction_id, row.count);
    }
  }
  return counts;
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-18 02:24:58Z)**_

I checked out PR #182 and reviewed it against issue #155. The main problem is that the branch has only about half of what the PR description says. The loot-core work is done (soft remove, restore, cleanup, merge), but the mobile transaction screen part was never pushed. So the description and the Test Evidence table describe files and tests that don't exist.

## Code Review Rubric — PR #182

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Correctness — does the change do what the issue asked? | 4 | The delete, undo, merge and cleanup work does what the issue asks. Deleted transactions' attachments are hidden and come back on undo, merges keep both sets, and cleanup removes rows before files and stops if another budget is opened. But only the paperclip from the mobile section is here. Nothing under `components/mobile/` opens the attachments window, and there's no "Attachments" field, "Take photo" button, viewer fit change or phone warning. That leaves 6 of the 7 mobile ACs unmet. Undo for a removal also can't be pressed while the attachments window is open (the PR's own "Known issue"), which is where people remove files. |
| Test coverage — are tests present and meaningful? | 6 | The loot-core tests are strong. `cleanup.test.ts` has 19 tests with a fake clock, covering undone deletes, closed vs. deleted accounts, running twice and failing partway through. There are also 4 merge tests, export, `delete-budget`, and restore. On the client, the Undo tests and 3 mobile list tests are meaningful. But several tests the PR lists aren't in the branch: the camera and photo tests, the phone warning test, `AttachmentViewerModal.test.tsx`, `e2e/attachments.mobile.test.ts`, and the new desktop e2e test for undoing a delete. |
| Code quality — consistent style, clear naming, no unnecessary duplication | 8 | The code is clean and well commented, and the cleanup steps are ordered so an interruption is safe.
